current_leader.name: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention engine
current_leader.state_transition: approved card authorization -> no matching clearing/reversal as scheme deadline approaches -> detect fee-triggering stale state -> recommend capture/reverse/leave based on merchant order state -> verify scheme integrity fee avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Visa and Mastercard impose explicit integrity/misuse fees when approved authorizations are not cleared or reversed within defined windows. PSPs expose authorization/capture/reversal states and APIs, creating independent triggers. A narrow read-only layer can identify stale authorizations and recommend the exact action before the fee deadline. Current searches found broad payment optimization and fee-audit products, but no dominant exact cross-PSP pre-deadline authorization-integrity fee prevention product.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: Mastercard raised/introduced multiple authorization-integrity fees in 2026, including time-based authorization validity fees; Visa misuse/integrity fees apply when approved authorizations lack timely matching clearing/reversal. Braintree explicitly warns to void unwanted authorizations to avoid misuse fees, while Adyen exposes reversal APIs and notes late captures can incur scheme/interchange fees.
current_leader.closest_threat: Broad payment-optimization/orchestration suites, interchange/scheme-fee auditors, and processor-native lifecycle tooling could absorb the feature. Some processors auto-expire authorizations, but expiry may occur after earlier card-network fee deadlines; exact PSP/network/MCC behavior remains to be mapped.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP authorization/capture/reversal webhooks plus merchant order/fulfillment state. Before each network deadline output CAPTURE NOW, REVERSE NOW, or NO ACTION with projected fee avoided. Keep execution merchant-confirmed or invoke the merchant's existing PSP endpoint under explicit authorization; do not route or custody funds.
current_leader.monetization: Per prevented-fee event, low monitoring fee, or capped percentage of verified scheme integrity fees avoided, reconciled against processor/network fee reports.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Processor-native auto-expiry/reversal may already prevent most exposure for common PSPs; fee rules vary by network, region, MCC and authorization type; broad enterprise payment-operations vendors may cover this narrow control without marketing it separately.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify integrity-fee incidence per 100k authorizations, map exact Visa/Mastercard deadlines by PSP/MCC/auth type, and attack competition for automatic stale-authorization reversal/pre-deadline fee prevention. Demote or reject if processors already neutralize most exposure or exact incumbent coverage is widespread.

recent_cross_family_findings: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention promoted to 50/60 because card networks impose explicit deadline-driven penalties on stale/unreversed authorizations and PSP lifecycle events create natural triggers.
Cloud support-plan right-sizing demoted to runner-up at 46/60 because support-tier decisions may be too static/annual and partly represent tail-risk insurance.
CPaaS idle-number release remains rejected: Twilio itself documents recurring number charges, inactivity checks, and API release as a first-party obvious optimization.
Business-domain renewal pruning rejected: multiple current portfolio tools already provide registrar sync, renewal cost tracking and cancellation/triage.
New rule: prefer explicit machine deadlines that create recurring penalty-avoidance events over annual rightsizing decisions.
New rule: processor auto-expiry is not equivalent to fee prevention unless it occurs before the applicable network fee deadline.
New rule: payment-network wedges may remain non-invasive if the product is read-only and uses merchant-confirmed existing PSP actions rather than becoming a routing proxy.
